record.title: Brazil opens a public selection for a national AI supercomputer led by LNCC
record.summary: The Brazilian National Laboratory for Scientific Computing (LNCC), a research unit of MCTI, reports that it is leading technical studies for a new AI-focused high-performance computer planned for Macaíba, Rio Grande do Norte, as part of the Brazilian AI Plan. The FACC official register lists Public Selection No. 27/2026 as an in-person procurement published on 20 August 2026 and closing on 4 November 2026, seeking integrated HPC for AI, research, technological development and innovation. LNCC’s report states a procurement value of R$ 959,040,959.04 and says the system is intended for model development, training and inference and to serve public agencies, researchers, universities and Brazil’s AI innovation ecosystem. The notice, terms and linked attachments did not load in this review. The available sources establish the planned procurement, not an award, delivered configuration, operational compute or measured performance.
organizations: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação
Fundação de Apoio ao Desenvolvimento da Computação Científica

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: LNCC reports that it is leading technical planning for a new AI-focused HPC system at the Augusto Severo Science and Technology Park in Macaíba, Rio Grande do Norte, as part of the Brazilian AI Plan. The announced site and project scope are reported by the responsible public laboratory.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The FACC official register lists Public Selection No. 27/2026 as an in-person procurement published on 20 August 2026, with the session/closing date on 4 November 2026, for an integrated HPC solution for AI, research, technological development and innovation. LNCC’s official report states a selection value of R$ 959,040,959.04. The notice, terms and attachments could not be fetched in this review; no award was verified.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The official report describes a planned procurement and intended use for model development, training and inference; it does not document a completed contract award, delivered hardware, available compute, operational performance, access conditions or energy consumption.

evidence_gaps.description: The FACC register links the edital, terms of reference and DOU notice, but all three PDFs failed to fetch in this review. Procurement specifications, contract duration and how the stated R$ 959,040,959.04 maps to the contract scope therefore remain unverified.
No completed award, final vendor/configuration, delivery schedule or operational status was verified.
The report provides no measured compute capacity, public access allocation, operating cost, energy use or realized research outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: If delivered and made available as intended, a public AI HPC system with a stated selection value near R$ 959 million could affect national research capacity and Brazil’s AI infrastructure strategy. Importance is bounded because the official report documents a procurement process, not an award, installed compute, access policy, energy footprint or realized outcomes.
limitations: The source is an official government laboratory report, but project plans and procurement figures are not evidence that a system has been awarded or commissioned.
The official procurement register was inspected, but the linked notice, terms and attachments failed to fetch; detailed scope and conditions remain unverified.
No vendor, contract award, delivered hardware, measured compute capacity, public-access terms, operating costs, energy use or outcomes were verified.
No vendor was identified or verified in this review.

The FACC official register lists Public Selection No. 27/2026 as an in-person procurement published on 20 August 2026 and closing on 4 November 2026, seeking integrated HPC for AI, research, technological development and innovation. LNCC’s report states a procurement value of R$ 959,040,959.04 and says the system is intended for model development, training and inference and to serve public agencies, researchers, universities and Brazil’s AI innovation ecosystem. technical.claimed_result: LNCC reports a public procurement step for an AI-focused HPC system in Macaíba, with a stated selection value of R$ 959,040,959.04; no system performance result is claimed.
technical.compute_or_cost: The official report states R$ 959,040,959.04 for the public selection object. It separately describes broader federal AI infrastructure announcements; those values should not be conflated. No operating cost or delivered compute capacity was reported in the reviewed source.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official report documents the project plan and selection stage. This review did not verify an award, installed system or operational results.
technical.implementation_status: An official FACC register lists the in-person procurement as open through 4 Nov 2026; the linked edital/terms/DOU PDFs failed to fetch. Award and commissioning were not verified.
technical.mechanism: LNCC leads technical specifications and implementation studies; the public selection seeks an integrated high-performance computing solution for AI research and development.
technical.regime: Planned national AI HPC infrastructure at Macaíba, Rio Grande do Norte, linked to Brazil’s federal Brazilian AI Plan. Intended users include government agencies, research institutions, universities and the AI innovation ecosystem.
technical.reproducibility: This is a policy/procurement development, not a performance claim. FACC’s register was inspected, but the linked edital and terms failed to fetch; later award/delivery records were not checked.
technical.strongest_baseline: Existing Santos Dumont scientific supercomputer in Petrópolis is described as continuing operation; the new planned system is additional infrastructure, not a replacement.

brief.title: Brazil opens a public selection for a national AI supercomputer led by LNCC
brief.why_it_matters: If procured and operated as described, the project could materially expand publicly oriented AI compute in Brazil and connect infrastructure spending with research, workforce development and technology transfer. Its realized capacity, access terms, energy use, cost and domestic capability effects remain unverified because the source reports a selection stage rather than an operating facility.
